jobs.title: Front End Developer
jobs.description: Remote Front End Developer About SchemeServe For 26 years, SchemeServe has helped transform insurance products into successful, profitable solutions. We’re always looking for new ways to innovate and improve. We strive to challenge industry norms and bring a unique personality to our work. In a nutshell, SchemeServe is a UK-based Insurance SaaS solution specialising in services for starting, managing, and growing traditional (and specialist) insurance products. It was started in 2000 by our CEO and Founder, Adam, and the software now represents the leading edge in super-fast scheme deployment and truly Obsessive Support ™. We’re fully remote, but we get together twice a year for some not-so-serious, and teeny tiny bit of serious, time together. We value self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and take on new challenges. To help with this, we offer learning budgets for courses, books, and workshops. Since we’re remote, we don’t offer free snacks or bean bags, but we do provide flexible work arrangements, a healthy work-life balance, and a friendly company culture. Every Thursday, we have 'Elevenses,' where anyone can join a video call to catch up, share stories, or play games. It helps us stay connected. About the role Enjoy the freedom of remote work while playing a key role in shaping the tools that thousands of brokers and insurers rely on. By enhancing our front-end, you'll improve user interfaces that empower professionals to manage schemes more efficiently and provide excellent service to their clients, all from the comfort of your home. If you're a passionate Front-end Developer in the UK who knows React.js and modern front-end tools, this opportunity could be an excellent fit for you. We’re looking for someone ready to jump in and focus on building user interfaces as part of one of our product teams. Within 6 to 12 months, you’ll help build and modernise core parts of SchemeServe, significantly enhancing our clients' workflow and efficiency.

jobs.description: About Nebius: Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The role Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on. Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production. Your responsibilities Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff. jobs.title: Backend Software Engineer, ML Inference
jobs.description: Who we are Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables. We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi . The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level. We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter , Noah Hollmann , and Sauraj Gambhir , and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years. About the role You will have ownership over designing, building, and scaling the core systems that bring Prior Labs' foundation models to the world. This is a unique opportunity to make fundamental architectural decisions, establish engineering best practices from the ground up, and profoundly shape the technical direction for serving state-of-the-art AI. TabPFN does its learning in the forward pass, and it now handles datasets in the millions of rows. Making that fast, reliable, and affordable is an exciting engineering challenge. You'll work directly with world-class AI researchers, translating cutting-edge models into scalable production systems. This role offers significant autonomy and impact, with clear paths to specialize in areas you're passionate about (like inference optimization and core backend systems) or grow into a technical leadership position as our team expands. jobs.description: About Boltz Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible. Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes. We focus on two things: Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners. Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment. The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich. You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto . jobs.description: Werde Teil unserer Mission, werde Teil von Doctolib! Wir suchen Dich als Technical Onboarding Engineer als Unterstützung für das Technical Onboarding Team in Berlin. Du verantwortest eigenständig die technischen Onboardings unseres KI-basierten Telefonassistenten und sorgst dafür, dass Praxen und Krankenhäuser von Tag 1 an reibungslos mit Doctolib arbeiten können. Dabei übernimmst Du Standard- und mittelkomplexe Implementierungen, von der Prüfung der technischen Voraussetzungen bis zur Übergabe in den laufenden Betrieb. In den ersten Monaten wächst Du in unsere Systeme hinein, betreust bald Deine eigenen Kund:innen und bringst Deine Ideen ein, um unser Onboarding Schritt für Schritt besser zu machen. Deine Aufgaben KI in die Praxis bringen: Du installierst, konfigurierst und testest unseren KI-gestützten Telefonassistenten bei Standard- und mittelkomplexen Implementierungen. So stellst Du sicher, dass er im Praxisalltag zuverlässig funktioniert. Eigene Onboardings steuern: Du planst Deine Onboardings, stimmst die nächsten Schritte mit Praxen und deren IT ab und behältst Zeitpläne und offene Punkte im Blick. Technische Voraussetzungen klären: Du prüfst gemeinsam mit den IT-Ansprechpartner:innen der Kund:innen Anforderungen rund um Telefonanlagen, Netzwerke, VPNs und Schnittstellen und gibst ihnen klare Orientierung. Daten sicher überführen: Du begleitest die Migration von Patienten- und Termindaten aus externen Praxissystemen in unsere Software. Dabei achtest Du darauf, dass die Daten richtig und vollständig sind. Probleme lösen und gezielt eskalieren: Du analysierst technische Fehler, findest die Ursachen und setzt passende Lösungen um. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Partner Integrations
jobs.description: About the team Most providers make customers migrate their data to them. We're doing the opposite: bringing ClickHouse Cloud into the environments our customers already trust, so their data stays useful right where it lives. Those environments come in a few shapes. Some are major cloud data platforms that run ClickHouse as a native service, so customers get it without leaving the tool they already use. Some are BI and visualization tools that need ClickHouse to show up as a fast, first-class data source behind their dashboards. And some are developer and data platforms we connect through marketplaces and identity federation with a couple of clicks or agentic calls. Every integration is unique, but the goal is the same every time: ClickHouse should feel like a first-class citizen in every environment. The craft is finding the patterns underneath different integrations. As one of the first backend engineers, you'll help shape the technical defaults for this team. You'll have end-to-end ownership, but you'll also work inside the constraints of platforms you don't own: thin documentation, unfamiliar deployment topologies, and timelines governed by partner approval cycles. A lot of the challenge is engineering across trust boundaries you don't fully control. You won't be doing it alone. You'll work closely with your engineering manager, the product manager, a growing team, and experienced engineers across the broader org. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, let's talk. jobs.title: FPGA Engineer Intern
jobs.description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About the Role As an FPGA Engineer Intern on Harmattan AI’s compute module team, you will take camera aggregation from concept to real hardware for the first time. Our drones carry more cameras than a single processor can take in, and your job is to show how an FPGA can close that gap. You will own the work end to end, from first design to a demonstrator on the bench. Your results will set how cameras are connected in our next hardware generation. Responsibilities Integrate existing IP cores, write HDL wrappers, simulate and validate FPGA logic that merges multiple camera streams into one. Investigate the system’s limits in camera count, resolution and frame rate. Build the processor-side pipeline that splits the merged stream so each camera stays independently usable. Debug the full chain, from cables and connectors to FPGA logic and camera software on the processor. Deliver a complete demonstrator and documentation that guide our next hardware design.
